title: Orbit operation picture, per-worker context, supervisor health/handoff, and state repair (issue #44)

lanes.title: Snapshot: operation picture (next items, idle reason), per-worker context, supervisor health, handoff state
acceptance_criteria: snapshot.build_snapshot keeps its current signature working and accepts optional inputs for the new sections; Snapshot additions (top-level keys, every value an evidence dict {label, value, timestamp, source, freshness} or a list of plain records): 'operation': {'actionable': [{id, kind, priority, summary, inspect}], 'others_waiting': [...same], 'blocked': [{id, kind, summary}], 'idle_reason': evidence, 'warnings': [str], 'fingerprint': str}; 'supervisor_health': {'lock_alive': evidence, 'last_tick_at': evidence, 'last_event_kind': evidence}; 'handoff': {'latest_id': evidence, 'verified': evidence, 'created_at': evidence}; each worker record gains 'context_pressure': {'tokens','window','ratio','level'} evidences (UNAVAILABLE with reason when its transcript is not found).

The operation section comes from dev_supervisor.autonomy (read-only import of its next computation); per-worker context pressure uses telemetry.find_transcript/context_pressure for each worker's session id and cwd (worktree)
Supervisor health from the state store lock and the events log (last tick or last event time); handoff state from the newest handoff file in the state directory and its verify status if recorded

New entry point `python -B -m dev_supervisor.snapshot --out <file> [--repo <root>]` builds the FULL snapshot (telemetry, registry, events, operation, health, handoff, account usage via telemetry.RateLimitEventProvider if that class exists, else UNAVAILABLE) and writes it atomically; read-only otherwise
At least 25 new offline tests; one OBSERVED live run of the entry point against the real state (counts only)
Synthetic data only: no real footage, no network in unit tests, no secrets/tokens/keys printed, stored or committed, no absolute user paths in tracked files
Any live observation is summarised as numbers and identifiers only, labelled OBSERVED with the exact command; anything not observed is NOT TESTED
Nothing is described as VERIFIED without command output; the lane report separates implemented, tested, observed, proposed and open items
Do NOT edit cli.py, launch.py, lifecycle.py, provider_env.py, telemetry.py or autonomy.py (claimed by open tasks or a merged lane); import them read-only
Full suite (cd orchestrator && python -B -I -m unittest discover -s tests) and the desktop node tests stay green; existing tests are not weakened

lanes.title: Supervisor state repair: retire stale authoritative Main records
acceptance_criteria: New module dev_supervisor/repair.py with CLI `python -B -m dev_supervisor.repair [--yes]`: finds sessions-document records with role main, authoritative true, status ACTIVE/RETIRING that are NOT main.json's RUNNING session and whose process is not alive (pid from the record or ~/.claude/sessions files via telemetry.read_sessions, liveness probe injectable) and proposes retiring them (authoritative false, status RETIRED_STALE, note with reason and time)

Dry run by default prints the plan; --yes applies it through StateStore atomic writes (backup kept), appends a 'state_repaired' event, and refuses when the supervisor lock is held by a live process unless --allow-while-running is given (then it only edits the sessions document, never main.json); never touches a session that is alive or is main.json's session; never deletes records

At least 20 offline tests (stale vs alive vs current, lock held, corrupt document, idempotent re-run); one OBSERVED live DRY RUN against the real state (ids shortened to 8 chars); do not run --yes on the real state (Main decides)
